description: Offline golden corpus for the zero-LLM problem-statement compression ladder (Phase B). Consumed by backend/tests/test_problem_compression_golden.py. Each case fixes the budget and asserts ladder properties: termination (output <= budget tokens), the Rung-0 byte-identical pin, lossless Rung-1 cleanup, and normative-first retention under the Rung-3 clamp. Token sizing reuses services.llm.usage.estimate_tokens (utf-8-byte basis). The builder assembles a statement from optional fields joined by a blank line, in this order: problem_statement_prefix, the fr_unit repeated fr_count times (one normative block), narrative_filler repeated narrative_repeat times (one narrative block), problem_statement_suffix. A literal 'problem_statement' overrides the builder.

cases.problem_statement: Build a team task tracker where users create projects, assign tasks, set due dates, comment, and see project status. FR-001: users must authenticate. FR-002: managers must approve task closure.

Build a CRM.



The   sales    team    needs    to    track    leads.

Page 1 of 12

FR-010: the system must record every lead source.

cases.problem_statement_prefix: Build a regulated healthcare scheduling platform. The following requirements are normative.
cases.fr_unit: - FR-{n:03d}: the system must enforce requirement {n} for patient records.
cases.narrative_filler: This is purely background narrative prose describing the history and motivation of the project, repeated to inflate the input past the budget.

cases.problem_statement_prefix: We have spent years thinking about this product and its market.
cases.narrative_filler: Background context and rationale that carries no requirement and may be dropped.
cases.problem_statement_suffix:
- FR-900: the export endpoint must stream as NDJSON.
- FR-901: every mutation must be audit-logged.

cases.fr_unit: - SEC-{n:03d}: the platform shall mitigate threat {n} with a documented control and review cadence.
